causalAutopsy.notes: The Stage B durable-delivery rollout fenced the stuck-input recovery keypress behind a delivery row; rows are prepared for codex-cli only, so the fence became unsatisfiable on every other framework. It stayed invisible because a refusal consumed no rung: the ladder never exhausted, so the escalation and give-up paths that would have raised something were unreachable. Measured 75,001 consecutive refusals, all at attempt 0. The second half — every terminal path ending in one JSONL row and nothing else — is older still and independent of the fence. I did not identify the Stage B PR number, so origin is recorded as latent rather than naming a PR I had not verified.

guardEvidence.howCaught: Steady-state bound: at most maxAttempts (4) keypresses per stuck prompt text, asserted over 40 consecutive ticks. Settling brake: a refusal now consumes the same budget (consecutiveRefusals), so the previously unbounded refusal loop (75,001 consecutive refusals measured, all at attempt 0) terminates; undeliverableRaised makes the terminal alarm one-shot per wedge; record.exhausted stops all further firing until the prompt text changes.
